# Infant Food Puree Vegetable

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="infant-food-puree-vegetable-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="infant-food-puree-vegetable-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="infant-food-puree-vegetable-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the infant Food Puree Vegetable came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-infant-food-puree-vegetable" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-infant-food-puree-vegetable-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of infant food puree vegetable, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="ingredients-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach infant Food Puree Vegetable

<a id="hmi-prd-010"></a>
<a id="which-ingredients-or-inputs-are-plausible-contributors-and-which-contributions-have-been-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-may-enter-during-manufacturing-handling-or-contact-with-equipment-and-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-012"></a>
<a id="how-do-formulation-ingredient-origins-and-product-format-alter-those-pathways"></a>

No study in the library compared infant Food Puree Vegetable from contaminated and ordinary settings, so the routes by which metals reach it are not measured here.



<a id="manufacturing-packaging-and-storage"></a>
## Manufacturing, packaging and storage

<a id="hmi-prd-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-manufacturing-and-preparation-change-concentrations-species-or-contaminant-mass"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-014"></a>
<a id="what-migration-or-release-from-equipment-or-packaging-has-been-measured-under-relevant-conditions"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-015"></a>
<a id="how-do-storage-duration-temperature-reuse-or-other-use-conditions-affect-contamination"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed infant Food Puree Vegetable in the same study and group. Infant Food Puree Vegetable, oil (Vegetables) had lead higher at 1.8 µg/kg, against 0.4 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (infant food puree vegetable, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis">Analytical Results for Lead in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children (FY2023)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.


<a id="exposure-from-infant-food-puree-vegetable"></a>
<a id="use-consumption-and-exposure"></a>
## Exposure from infant Food Puree Vegetable

<a id="hmi-prd-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-serving-size-consumption-frequency-preparation-or-non-food-use-determine-exposure"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-017"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-addresses-intended-users-and-susceptible-or-highly-exposed-populations"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-018"></a>
<a id="what-do-exposure-estimates-establish-and-what-cannot-be-inferred-about-health-effects-or-individual-risk"></a>

No source in the library converted infant Food Puree Vegetable concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.

<a id="levers-to-reduce-contamination"></a>
## Mitigation for infant Food Puree Vegetable

<a id="hmi-prd-019"></a>
<a id="which-interventions-have-been-evaluated-in-this-exact-product-or-a-demonstrably-applicable-setting"></a>
<a id="hmi-prd-020"></a>

<a id="hmi-prd-021"></a>
<a id="which-measures-prevent-remove-redistribute-dilute-detect-or-exclude-contamination-and-how-are-they-verified"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 3 µg/kg (Parker et al. 2022) to 30 µg/kg (Kirkpatrick et al. 1980), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Infant Food Puree Vegetable FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-infant-food-puree-vegetable" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-infant-food-puree-vegetable" data-question="What heavy metals are found in infant Food Puree Vegetable?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in infant Food Puree Vegetable?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, B, Ba, Ca, K, Li, Mg, Mo, Na and Sr in infant Food Puree Vegetable, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/parker2022-baby-food-arsenic-cadmium-lead-mercury-risk|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Parker GH, Gillie CE, Miller JV, Badger DE, Kreider ML · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/parker2022-baby-food-arsenic-cadmium-lead-mercury-risk">Human health risk assessment of arsenic, cadmium, lead, and mercury ingestion from baby foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/parker2022-baby-food-arsenic-cadmium-lead-mercury-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Spungen JH, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium">Infants&#39; and young children&#39;s dietary exposures to lead and cadmium: FDA total diet study 2018-2020</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fadhel2023-baghdad-baby-food-lead-cadmium|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fadhel JF, Ghathwan MA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fadhel2023-baghdad-baby-food-lead-cadmium">Detection of Lead (Pb) and Cadmium (Cd) Concentrations and Hazards in Some Baby Food Samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Ibn Al-Haitham Journal for Pure and Applied Sciences 36(4), 2023, pp. 127-136</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fadhel2023-baghdad-baby-food-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kirkpatrick1980-trace-elements-canadian-baby-foods|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kirkpatrick DC, Conacher HBS, Méranger JC, Dabeka R, Collins B, McKenzie AD, Lacroix GMA, Savary G · 1980</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kirkpatrick1980-trace-elements-canadian-baby-foods">The Trace Element Content of Canadian Baby Foods and Estimation of Trace Element Intake by Infants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Canadian Institute of Food Science and Technology Journal 13(4):154-161</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kirkpatrick1980-trace-elements-canadian-baby-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-infant-food-puree-vegetable-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-infant-food-puree-vegetable-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of infant Food Puree Vegetable measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of infant Food Puree Vegetable measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 9 groups of infant Food Puree Vegetable ranged from 390 µg/kg (retail product Fv17 (vegetable-based), Baghdad local market) to 1,100 µg/kg (retail product Fv11 (vegetable-based), Baghdad local market); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fadhel2023-baghdad-baby-food-lead-cadmium|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fadhel JF, Ghathwan MA · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fadhel2023-baghdad-baby-food-lead-cadmium">Detection of Lead (Pb) and Cadmium (Cd) Concentrations and Hazards in Some Baby Food Samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Ibn Al-Haitham Journal for Pure and Applied Sciences 36(4), 2023, pp. 127-136</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fadhel2023-baghdad-baby-food-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, total arsenic across 14 groups of infant Food Puree Vegetable ranged from 0.48 µg/kg (puree product 16 (manufacturer category E)) to 7.81 µg/kg (puree product 33 (manufacturer category D)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Brian P. Jackson, Vivien F. Taylor, Tracy Punshon, Kathryn L. Cottingham · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods">Arsenic concentration and speciation in infant formulas and first foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pure and Applied Chemistry, Vol. 84, No. 2, pp. 215-223</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-infant-food-puree-vegetable" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-infant-food-puree-vegetable" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in infant Food Puree Vegetable?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in infant Food Puree Vegetable?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same infant Food Puree Vegetable.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis">Analytical Results for Lead in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children (FY2023)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Infant Food Puree Vegetable, oil (Vegetables) had lead higher at 1.8 µg/kg, against 0.4 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (infant food puree vegetable, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis">Analytical Results for Lead in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children (FY2023)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2024-lead-baby-food-fy2023-guidance-basis">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
